ruylopez.idea: Pressure on e5 through the knight that guards it, building towards c3 and d4.
ruylopez.White: Castle, Re1, c3 and d4 for a big centre; the b3 bishop and a later Nbd2-f1-g3 aim at the kingside.
ruylopez.Black: Hold e5, play ...b5 to gain space, and strike back with ...d5 or ...c5 once developed.

italiangame.idea: Quick development with the bishop on f7's diagonal, then a fight over d4.
italiangame.White: Either c3 and d4 for a big centre, or a slow d3 build-up with Re1, Nbd2-f1-g3 and a kingside push.
italiangame.Black: Develop fast, keep e5, and break with ...d5 when White's centre is not ready for it.

kingsgambit.idea: A pawn for the centre and an open f-file aimed at Black's king.
kingsgambit.White: Play d4 and Bc4, castle, and attack f7 down the f-file; regain the f4 pawn when it's convenient.
kingsgambit.Black: Either hold the pawn with ...g5, or return it with ...d5 for free development.

viennagame.idea: Develop the knight first, then decide between f4 attacks and quiet fianchetto play.
viennagame.White: Prepare f4 to open the f-file, or fianchetto with g3 and Bg2 to press on d5.
viennagame.Black: Challenge with ...d5 at the right moment; it frees Black's game in almost every line.

queensgambit.idea: Use the c-pawn to pull Black's d-pawn from the centre and gain space.
queensgambit.White: Pressure d5 with Nc3, Bg5 and Rc1; in the Exchange, push b4–b5 against Black's queenside.
queensgambit.Black: Hold d5 solidly, then free the game with ...c5 or ...e5 before White's pressure grows.

catalan.idea: A Queen's Gambit with the light bishop on g2, pressing the long diagonal.
catalan.White: Castle, then Qc2, Rd1 and e4; regain c4 if Black took it, and keep the bishop's pressure on b7.
catalan.Black: Hold d5 or take on c4, then free the c8 bishop with ...b6 or ...c5 without weakening c6.

london.idea: The same solid setup against almost anything: d4, Bf4, e3, Nf3, c3, Bd3 and Nbd2.
london.White: Build the pyramid, castle, then use Ne5 and a kingside attack, or a well-timed e4 or c4 break.
london.Black: Strike early with ...c5 and ...Qb6 against b2, or swap off the f4 bishop with ...Bd6.

englishopening.idea: Control the centre from the flank, usually with g3, Bg2 and Nc3.
englishopening.White: Press the long diagonal and d5, expand on the queenside with Rb1 and b4, and keep e4 in reserve.
englishopening.Black: Take central space with ...e5 or ...d5, and avoid letting the g2 bishop dominate.

sicilian.idea: An unbalanced fight: Black trades the c-pawn for White's d-pawn and plays on the c-file.
sicilian.White: Use the lead in development: f3, Be3, Qd2 and O-O-O with a pawn storm, or Bc4 aimed at f7.
sicilian.Black: Counterattack on the queenside with ...a6, ...b5 and rooks on c8, and look for ...d5 to free the game.

french.idea: A solid e6–d5 chain: Black accepts less space and hits back at White's centre.
french.White: Gain space with e5 and attack the kingside; keep d4 well defended.
french.Black: Undermine d4 with ...c5 and ...Qb6, then ...f6 against e5; find a role for the c8 bishop.

carokann.idea: A rock-solid c6–d5 structure with the light bishop developed outside it.
carokann.White: Use extra space: e5 and kingside play in the Advance, or h4–h5 against the f5 bishop.
carokann.Black: Get the bishop out, then ...e6, ...c5 and queenside play; aim for a healthy endgame.

pirc.idea: Hypermodern: allow White's centre, then attack it with pieces and pawn breaks.
pirc.White: Use the space: f4 and e5, or Be3, Qd2, Bh6 and a kingside attack.
pirc.Black: Fianchetto, castle, then break with ...e5 or ...c5 before White's attack lands.

modern.idea: Maximum flexibility: Black waits to see White's setup before choosing a pawn break.
modern.White: Build a broad centre and use the space, but don't over-extend.
modern.Black: Fianchetto, then hit the centre with ...c5, ...e5 or ...d5, or expand with ...a6 and ...b5.

alekhine.idea: Provocation: Black lets White's pawns chase the knight, then attacks them.
alekhine.White: Keep the centre supported and use the space; don't push pawns that can't be defended.
alekhine.Black: Undermine e5 and d4 with ...d6, ...c5 and piece pressure, then exploit the weaknesses left behind.

scandinavian.idea: Clear the centre early and develop smoothly, even at the cost of a tempo.
scandinavian.White: Gain time on the queen, develop with d4, Nf3 and Bc4, and use the extra space.
scandinavian.Black: Develop the c8 bishop before ...e6, play ...c6 for a solid shell, and avoid queen traps.

petrov.idea: Symmetry and solidity: Black mirrors White to reach a safe, balanced position.
petrov.White: Use the small lead in development: d4, Bd3, castle, and Re1 against the e4 knight.
petrov.Black: Regain the pawn safely, keep the e4 knight supported with ...d5, and develop symmetrically.

philidor.idea: A compact, solid shell around e5, giving White space but few targets.
philidor.White: Use the space: develop quickly, castle, and look for breaks against e5 or f7.
philidor.Black: Hold e5 with ...Nbd7, ...Be7 and ...c6, then expand with ...b5 or break with ...exd4.

kingsindian.idea: Let White build a big centre, then hit it with ...e5 and attack on the kingside.
kingsindian.White: Keep the centre, close it with d5 when it suits, and attack on the queenside with c5.
kingsindian.Black: Play ...e5, then often ...Nh5 and ...f5 for a kingside attack once the centre is locked.

nimzoindian.idea: Fight for e4 with pieces, ready to trade the bishop for doubled pawns on c3.
nimzoindian.White: Win the bishop pair, keep the centre, and open the position for the bishops.
nimzoindian.Black: Control e4, target doubled c-pawns, and keep the position closed so knights shine.

queensindian.idea: Control e4 from b7, keeping a solid position with no weaknesses.
queensindian.White: Fight for e4 with Nc3 and Qc2, and use the extra queenside space.
queensindian.Black: Hold e4 with the b7 bishop and knight, then free the game with ...c5 or ...d5.

grunfeld.idea: Let White take the centre with pawns, then attack it with pieces and ...c5.
grunfeld.White: Build the e4–d4 centre, support it, and push d5 when it gains space.
grunfeld.Black: Hit d4 with the g7 bishop, ...c5 and ...Nc6, and exploit any loosening of White's centre.

slav.idea: Hold d5 with ...c6 so the c8 bishop can still develop outside the pawn chain.
slav.White: Pressure d5, regain c4 if Black takes it, and use the space for e4.
slav.Black: Develop the bishop to f5 or g4, then ...e6; break with ...c5 or ...e5 when ready.

benoni.idea: Unbalance the game: White gets central space, Black gets queenside and dark-square play.
benoni.White: Use the central majority to push e4–e5, and keep Black's queenside play in check.
benoni.Black: Use the queenside majority and open files with ...b5, and the long diagonal with ...Bg7.

dutch.idea: Control e4 with the f-pawn and play for a kingside attack.
dutch.White: Fianchetto, fight for e4 with Nc3 and Qc2, and exploit the loosened e6 and e5 squares.
dutch.Black: Hold e4, then attack with ...Qe8–h5 or ...g5, or the Stonewall's ...Ne4 and ...Qe7.
